answer: An agent economy can gate valuable actions through a stake-weighted challenge period: an agent posts collateral, and any participant can bridge evidence of duplicate control to an independent verifier. The verifier checks signed task histories against a shared kernel of identity commitments; a matching signal lets challengers slash the bond and block withdrawal. Creating many names is still possible, but each must lock capital, remain exposed through the review window, and risk losing its stake, making mass Sybil identities costly rather than merely cheap account creation.
